correctness.rationale: Read RESULT.md full Hermite divided-difference/confluent-residue proof. The simplex Fourier integral equals (-2pi i)^(-5) times fifth divided difference of exp(-2pi i t) at the six integer barycentric frequency nodes. All distinct nodes give zero by constant interpolation. For multiplicities, each integer-node residue is a rational-coefficient polynomial in c=2pi i (all exp(-c*x)=1); since pi is transcendental, zero of that polynomial is equivalent to vanishing of each rational coefficient. A unique node with multiplicity >=3 forces an uncancelled high-degree c coefficient; types 3+3 and 2+2+2 have nonzero linear c coefficient. The only possible repeated-node zero type is 2+2+1+1, where cancellation of the two simple double-node residue coefficients occurs only for doubled positions (0,2) or (1,3), producing precisely the two gap equations. Algebraically these give divisibility parameterizations delta=r-p | 2p^2 and its reflection. An independently implemented rational formal-residue algorithm checked all 1287 integer-node six-multisets with min 0 and nodes in [0,8], matching exactly the classified families. This check is finite; exhaustive partition/degree argument proves all integer nodes.

value.rationale: Gives an exact arithmetic description of all lattice Fourier zeros for a canonical dimension-five polytope, including two infinite and nontrivial repeated-knot families that simple all-distinct vanishing does not capture. Useful for spectral and tiling/cubature questions involving integer Fourier data.

final_claim: For the standard five-simplex and integer frequency k, its Fourier integral vanishes exactly when the six barycentric nodes {0,k1,...,k5} are all distinct, or are integer-translates of {0,0,p,p+q,p+q,p+q+r} with qr=p(p+q+r), or {0,p,p,p+q,p+q+r,p+q+r} with pq=r(p+q+r), p,q,r positive integers.
limitations: Only standard 5-simplex, integer frequencies and ordinary Lebesgue measure under e^(-2pi i kx).
Transcendence of pi used for polynomial noncancellation; finite test range not universal evidence.
Earlier equivalent exponential divided-difference classification remains possible.
